title: OpenAlarm visual identity
question: All four boards show List (light/dark), Editor, Ringing, Ringing with Phase Two tasks, and Nightstand. Pick a direction, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Travel Clock
options.thesis: The app is the clock's flat plastic body; every time sits in a small reflective LCD window set into it.
options.viewport: Large title, one 'Next Mon 06:30 · in 7 h 16 min' line, then rows: LCD window with slanted segment time, label and days, yellow switch.
options.risk: Can tip into Braun pastiche if body textures or knurls creep in; the LCD window per row is the one container the design allows.

raised.raise: One message only above the list: the next alarm and the time until it.
Rows carry no card, divider, or chrome except the LCD window itself.
Segment stroke width is the base unit: spacing, corner radii, and window inset derive from it.
Two text sizes plus the segment display; hierarchy comes from ink, not size.
Disabled alarms fade toward unlit segments, so on/off reads at a glance.

options.label: Unlit Glass
options.lineage: reflective LCD watch and calculator glass
options.thesis: The whole screen is one unlit LCD; every state is a printed segment that is either inked or ghosted.
materials: annunciator legends (M T W T F S S, LOUD, AL, SNZ)
options.viewport: Big unboxed segment times on the LCD ground; under each, the label and a fixed weekday annunciator strip with active days inked, inactive ghosted.
options.risk: Most literal reading of the brief and the look most runs would land on; light mode's green ground needs care to keep text contrast at 4.5:1.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: rail concourse split-flap boards, rendered in LCD segments
options.thesis: Alarms as a timetable: fixed columns, rows ranked by time, each digit in its own cell, the next alarm called in amber.
options.viewport: Column heads TIME / ALARM / ON, then ruled rows of celled digits; the next alarm has an amber lamp and 'NEXT · 7 H 16 MIN'.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: an alarm list is literally a time-ranked board, and the call lamp makes 'next' unmistakable. Loses on audience: transit, not bedroom.
options.risk: Fixed columns get tight at large Dynamic Type sizes and with long labels in other languages.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.case: Saturated yellow glares in a dark bedroom; sleepers do not identify with airports.
options.kept: One message per band: the next decision only.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.case: Tiles add color fields with no job; reads as a dated phone OS.
options.kept: Chrome deleted so the type itself is the interface.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.case: Visible grid lines are decoration without a job, against the brief.
options.kept: Letterforms and layout built from the same grid tokens.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Layered leaves and tabs add depth an alarm list never needs.
options.kept: One size does the work; rank comes from layer, not scale.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.case: Alarms have no artwork; horizontal rails hide alarms off screen.
options.kept: The item that matters grows; everything else steps back.

canonCard.label: Clock app, played straight
canonCard.thesis: What the category ships: system grouped lists, thin rounded digits, orange tint, no segment display.
canonCard.viewport: Apple Clock's alarm list at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Apple Clock and ignores the 7-segment brief.
